scope: One focused private negative test of the production-coupled MIME Reader runner. It proves that the runner rejects the retired direct-parse profile producer after that producer's core test passes and before either the Tauri or React stage starts. This is not a full source, native WebKit, provider, package, release, or Phase 2 result.

mutation.semanticChange: The selected core test was changed from mail::tests::mime_reader_handoff_tests::public_full_and_selective_reader_fetches_preserve_every_governed_reader_fixture to mail::tests::mime_tauri_artifact_export_tests::governed_mime_fixtures_export_a_real_reader_profile_for_tauri.
mutation.nonSemanticImportChange: The sourceSnapshot import was rebound to the absolute primary helper because the private mutant ran outside the repository scripts directory.

rejection.message: core MIME profile artifact has the wrong identity or producer

retainedWrongProducerArtifact.observedMismatch: The legacy manifest has no producer or profileState field and carries direct-parse UIDs 701 through 709. The coupled producer uses MailService hydration, a closed-and-reopened profile state, and UIDs 800 through 808.

earlierHarnessCaptureError.description: The first mutant execution reached the same expected producer rejection, but the surrounding zsh recorder used the reserved variable name status. It is retained and is not the final exit-code evidence.

review.finding: Independent review confirmed that the mutation was limited to the producer selection and required out-of-tree import rebind, the legacy core producer passed, the coupled runner rejected its manifest before downstream stages, the expected nonzero exit was recorded, and the source tree was unchanged.

limitations: This focused result does not rerun or alter the earlier successful same-profile provider-to-Reader result.
The direct-parse core exporter remains present for its older standalone purpose. This result proves only that the coupled runner rejects it as a production hydration artifact.
The orchestrator subprocess has no explicit wall-clock timeout.
No full source, native WebKit, external provider, user mailbox, package, release, performance, fuzz, dependency-audit, or Phase 2 result is claimed.
